results.title: Importance of markers in the standardization of herbal drugs
results.content: This review highlights the importance of standardized methods and the role of marker compounds in achieving the consistent quality necessary for effective herbal drug development. By focusing on marker compounds, standardization can help minimize variance in quality, ensuring reproducibility in herbal medicine efficacy. The standardization of herbal drugs is essential for ensuring their quality, safety, and efficacy, and marker compounds play a pivotal role in this process. Standardization ensures consistent quality, safety, and efficacy of herbal medicines by verifying potency and identity through marker compounds. It is crucial for ensuring that herbal medicines are safe, effective, and consistent in their therapeutic effects, requiring meticulous identification and standardization of their chemical markers. The study of herbal medicine highlights the importance of standardization and quality control in ensuring their therapeutic effectiveness and safety, particularly when derived from complex natural sources. In herbal medicine, the scientific study involves validating traditional uses of plants, discovering active compounds, and developing standards for quality and efficacy, thereby bridging traditional knowledge with contemporary holistic practices. In herbal medicine, studies are conducted to identify active compounds, understand their mechanisms of action, and develop methods for standardization and quality assessment, ultimately ensuring that herbal products are safe and effective for consumer use. In reviewing herbal medicine, providing an account of standards and practices, particularly regarding the use and assessment of marker compounds, is vital for ensuring safety, quality, and efficacy in these products. Her contributions to the field of herbal research are significant, particularly in understanding the importance of standardization and markers in herbal medicines for ensuring quality control and therapeutic efficacy. In herbal medicine, understanding the pharmacological properties of various plant constituents is essential for developing effective treatments and ensuring that herbal products meet safety and efficacy standards. In the context of herbal medicine, knowledge is vital for identifying effective therapeutic applications, ensuring proper handling and processing of plants, and employing standardization practices to secure product quality and consumer safety. Researching neem highlights the necessity of chemical markers for quality assurance and the potential benefits of standardization to ensure that its use remains both effective and safe in herbal medicine. Home » FINGERPRINTING ANALYSIS AND MARKER COMPOUNDS IN QUALITY ASSESSMENT OF PHYTOPHARMACEUTICALS. #### FINGERPRINTING ANALYSIS AND MARKER COMPOUNDS IN QUALITY ASSESSMENT OF PHYTOPHARMACEUTICALS. Since decades, human beings have been utilizing plants to fulfill their food, medicine, and shelter needs. In the modern era plants, plant-derived products are developed as medicine and drug containing phytoconstituents by combining traditional knowledge and modern technologies. The presence of these phytoconstituents is needed to validate qualitatively and quantitatively to serve the purpose of the development of ‘phytopharmaceutical’. To achieve this, explicit plant species, the exact amount of phytoconstituents to show efficacy is required, *i.e.,* quality control of the drug is crucial. Hence, this review focuses on different quality control attributes of herbal material and related products to develop as a ‘pharmaceutical drug’. Considering marker compounds and fingerprint analysis as the main characteristic features for maintaining the quality of herbal drugs, this review has been designed. Using these features, falsification is detected in crude drugs, extracts, and final products with the application of different spectroscopic, chromatographic techniques. Thus, this review has quoted the use of reliable, efficient analytical tools through recapitulation of different case studies of adulteration detection of plant material, determination of phytoconstituents present in extracts, and formulations using chromatographic and spectroscopic methods to provide a quality assessment. # Article Information. results.title: Use of Fingerprinting and Marker Compounds for Identification and Standardization of Botanical Drugs: Strategies for Applying Pharmaceutical HPLC Analysis to Herbal Products | Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science
results.content: # Use of Fingerprinting and Marker Compounds for Identification and Standardization of Botanical Drugs: Strategies for Applying Pharmaceutical HPLC Analysis to Herbal Products. * Volume 32, pages 497–512, (1998). For standardization of natural product drugs, single chemical entities, “marker compounds, “ may be used as potency standards in high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis. Using well-characterized marker compounds, conventional pharmaceutical manufacturing criteria for assay and content uniformity may be applied. These marker compounds may be used to help identify herbal materials, set specifications for raw materials, standardize botanical preparations during all aspects of manufacturing processes, and obtain stability profiles. HPLC analysis for marker compounds may provide additional information in the form of “chromatographic fingerprints.” Examples discussed include valerian (Valeriana officinalis) and feverfew (Tanacetum parthenium). An intent of this paper is to illustrate how, in certain instances, chromatographic fingerprinting and markers can by used to make consistent herbal drug products. results.title: (PDF) Role of Chemical Marker in Quality Control of Herbal Drugs
results.content: The growing global interest in herbal medicine has heightened the demand for scientifically validated, standardized, and high-quality plant-based therapeutics. In this context, the application of chemical markers has emerged as a critical and scientifically sound approach for the quality control and standardization of herbal drugs. Chemical markers are defined as phytochemical constituents that serve as qualitative and/or quantitative indicators of the identity, purity, and potency of herbal materials. These markers are categorized broadly into three types: active markers (directly responsible for therapeutic effects), analytical markers (easily quantifiable and indicative of quality), and synergistic markers (compounds that contribute to efficacy through interaction with other constituents). results.title: Role of Markers in Standardization of Herbal Products | PPTX
results.content: It emphasizes 'marker-based standardization' as a method for ensuring consistent potency and quality of herbal medicines, while addressing challenges such as variability in raw materials, identification, and quality assurance. Role of Chemical& Biological Markers in Standardization of Herbal Products By Dr. Jitendra Patel Associate Professor AIPS, Hyderabad, India. • Standardization of herbal products is essential for their acceptance of herbal products as remedies for various diseases and ailments.It is necessary to establish consistent potency from batch to batch and to control the full spectrum of bioactive chemical constituent/s (biomarker/s), naturally occurring in medicinal plants. • Recently, the concept of marker-based standardization of herbal drugs is gaining momentum. • A marker compound is a chemically defined constituent of an herbal drug with or without therapeutic activity; It serves as a reference for standardizing test materials and can therefore be used for the quality assurance of a finished product. • Herbal medicinal products may vary in composition and properties, unlike conventional pharmaceutical products, which are usually prepared from synthetic, chemically pure materials by means of reproducible manufacturing techniques and procedures. • Standardization of herbal formulations is essential in order to assess the quality of drugs, based on the concentration of their active principles. OR • Markers are chemically defined constituents of a herbal drug which are of interest for quality control purposes independent of whether they have any therapeutic activity or not. Markers may serve to calculate the amount of active component of herbal drug or preparation in the finished product. • The quantity of a chemical marker can be an indicator of the quality of an herbal medicine. • The study of chemical markers is applicable to many research areas, including authentication of genuine species, search for new resources or substitutes of raw materials, optimization of extraction and purification methods, structure elucidation and purity determination. Chemical markers should be used at various stages of the development and manufacturing of an herbal medicine, such as authentication and differentiation of species, collecting and harvesting, quality evaluation and stability assessment, diagnosis of intoxication and discovery of lead compounds. • Lack of chemical markers remains a major problem for the quality control of herbal medicines.
